titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 3/2013 (ދައުލަތުގެ ވިޔަފާރިތައް ޚާއްސަ ކުރުމާއި ކޯޕަރޭޓް ކުރުމާއި ބެލެހެއްޓުމާއި ތަޙްލީލު ކުރުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިސްލާހު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Privatization and Corporatization, Monitoring and Evaluation of Government Businesses Act (Law No. 3/2013). It adds a new sub-article after an existing paragraph of Article 12. The new provision deals with performance reports of state-owned businesses, including a time limit of 90 days and another of 30 days, and a fine of MVR 5,000 for breaking the rules. The scans are hard to read, so some details are uncertain.
whyItMatters: If passed, state-owned companies would face a clear duty and deadlines to report on their performance, and a fine if they do not, so the public could see how government businesses are doing.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 adds a new sub-article to Article 12 of the Act, numbered as a '-1' paragraph after an existing paragraph.
Sub-article (1) sets out a duty for government businesses connected to a performance report, with a period of 1 year mentioned.
Sub-article (2) sets a time limit of 90 days.
Sub-article (3) sets a shorter time limit of 30 days.
Sub-article (4) says that failing to comply with (1) to (3) can be punished with a fine of MVR 5,000.
Clause 2 is a short commencement clause, saying when the amendment takes effect once it is ratified and published.
whoIsAffected: State-owned companies and the people who run them, the bodies that oversee them, and citizens who want to track how public money is used.
statedReasons: The explanatory note refers to performance reports of government businesses and to transparency and accountability.
